summary: Said Reza Huseini works in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Leiden University, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and King's College London.

Saiyid Athar Abbas Rizvi was a historian of religion who studied under Mohammad Habib and graduated from Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar University. He held posts at AMU, SOAS, University of Jammu and Kashmir, JNU, and the Australian National University (1967-1986).

Sakda Hemthep works in Buddhist studies. He earned an MPhil from Cardiff University in 2014 under Max Deeg, studied under Peter Harvey, and was attested as a PhD researcher at Ghent University in 2026.

Sakkottai Krishnaswamy Aiyangar was an Indologist and historian who earned degrees at the University of Madras. He lectured at Bangalore University (1899-1909) and held the Chair of Indian History and Archæology at the University of Madras (1914-1929).

Sakunoshin Motoda worked in religious studies. He studied at Kenyon College, the University of Pennsylvania, and Columbia University, later serving on the faculty at Rikkyo University from around 1899 to 1923.
Sakutaro Fujioka was a scholar of Japanology and history. He studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1894 to 1897 and later held a post there from around 1902 until 1910.
Sakya Trizin is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who founded Sakya College and taught Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse Rinpoche. He served as Abbot of Sakya Monastery until 2017.

Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies figure who studied under the 14th Dalai Lama, Khenpo Appey, and others. He founded the Sakya Centre, Sakya College, and Sakya Institute, teaching students including Sam van Schaik.

Sakyong Mipham is a Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology figure. He studied at Oxford, Namdroling Monastery, and under Chögyam Trungpa, whom he later succeeded. He also served on the board of Naropa University until 2018.

Sallie B. King specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. She studied at the University of British Columbia under Leon Hurvitz and served as a professor and later Professor Emerita of Philosophy and Religion at James Madison University.

Sally J. Sutherland Goldman is an Indologist who earned her PhD from UC Berkeley in 1979 under Shivram Dattatray Joshi and T. Shrinivas Shastri. She held posts at UC Berkeley, where she is attested as Senior Lecturer Emerita.
Sally McAra specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her MA at the University of Auckland (1999-2000), where she was supervised by Christine Dureau and Karen Nero.
Sally Mellick Cutler is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She earned a D.Phil. from the University of Oxford in 1993 and served as manager of the Pali Text Society Office, attested in 1997.

Salomon Lefmann was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Franz Bopp and at Berlin, Münster, Heidelberg, and Paris. He spent his career at Heidelberg University, becoming an associate professor in 1870 and honorary professor in 1901.

Saloni Mathur is an Indologist and art historian. She has held posts at the University of California, Los Angeles, serving as Associate Professor of Art History in 2011 and later as Professor and Chair of the Department of Art History.

Salvador E. Luria studied at the University of Turin, Sapienza University of Rome, and Columbia University. He held academic posts at Columbia, Indiana University Bloomington, the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (circa 1950-1959), and MIT (circa 1959-1991).

Sam Harris is a scholar in philosophy and religious studies. He studied philosophy at Stanford University, completed a PhD at UCLA, and trained under traditional teachers including Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje, and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche.

Sam van Schaik specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Manchester and studied under Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga. His posts include SOAS and the British Library's Endangered Archives Programme.
Samani Pratibha Pragya works in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. She completed her PhD at SOAS University of London and was attested as a research assistant there in 2020.
Sambhavi Ganesh is a scholar in Indology. She was attested in 2026 as a doctoral student at the University of Edinburgh under the supervision of Radhika Govinda.
